title: Smart Schema Adapter: Missing-Parameter Reconciliation and Suggestive Error Payloads
creator: Asha Menon
description: Problem: When model-driven tool/function calls emit incomplete or mis-shaped JSON payloads, downstream runtimes return opaque errors that are hard for application developers to remediate. This increases support load and can cause feature regressions in streaming and function-calling flows. Goal: Implement a Smart Schema Adapter in the serving runtime that (1) detects missing/incorrect parameters earlier, (2) augments error responses with structured, actionable repair hints and prioritized suggested fixes, and (3) supports compatibility shims that optionally auto-fill or transform legacy tool payloads for backwards compatibility with older SDKs. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, and a canary rollout for the adapter and the new error payload format.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a new error envelope type 'repairable_schema_error' for function/tool-call failures
Error envelope includes: missing_fields (list), suggested_fixes (list), schema_alternatives (list), confidence_score (0-1 string), and guidance_link
Adapter can run in three modes: 'detect-only', 'suggest-and-log', and 'auto-adapt' (configurable per-customer and per-route)

When running in 'auto-adapt', adapter applies deterministic, well-logged transforms (e.g., coercing numeric strings to numbers, filling boolean defaults per schema) and emits telemetry for each transform applied
SDKs (node/python) can surface suggested_fixes to developers via error wrappers without breaking existing error shapes (compatibility layer applied)
No measurable latency regression for p95 token-serving < 2ms at the adapter decision point in detect-only mode (bench to baseline)
End-to-end integration test covering streaming function calls where the model emits partial JSON then a repair hint produces valid invocation
design_notes: Error envelope chosen over ad-hoc strings to enable programmatic remediation and A/B testing of repair UX

Suggest fixes prioritized by heuristic score: schema proximity (Levenshtein of field names), type-coercion likelihood (based on observed distributions), and recent user-corrections (from opt-in telemetry)
Compatibility shim rules are explicit declarative transforms (JSONPath-based) stored per-model/version to avoid arbitrary mutation of user payloads
We will avoid automatic deletion of user-supplied keys; transforms should be additive or type-correcting unless running in a strict opt-in 'aggressive-adapt' customer mode
Trade-off: richer suggested_fixes increases payload size and client parsing work; mitigate by allowing max payload size and a 'compact' flag in error envelope
Security: any auto-fill that uses customer defaults must be gated behind customer config and logged; no secret material should be synthesized
implementation_plan: 1) Schema Comparator Library: implement a small runtime utility to compare emitted JSON against tool JSON Schema and produce a ranked list of missing/mismatched fields
2) Repair Hint Generator: map comparator output to human-readable suggested_fixes and machine-actionable transforms (expressed as JSON Patch operations)
3) Error Envelope Extension: add 'repairable_schema_error' to runtime error types and wire through API surfaces (hosted API, dedicated, private control plane)
4) Compatibility Shim Engine: implement declarative transform runner with safe whitelist operations (coerce, default, rename, nest/unnest) and opt-in config per route/customer
5) SDK Adaptors: update Node & Python SDKs to unwrap the new error envelope and expose 'suggested_fixes' as a first-class property on exceptions (backwards compatible wrapper)
6) E2E tests + fuzzing harness that generates mis-shaped payloads and validates adapter suggestions and applied transforms
7) Canary rollout: internal + 5 pilot customers using 'suggest-and-log', collect telemetry and developer feedback, then enable 'auto-adapt' for opt-in customers
test_plan: Unit tests for Schema Comparator (coverage for arrays, nested objects, union types)
Integration tests: streaming function call where model emits partial JSON across multiple chunks; adapter must reconstruct and detect missing params post-stream
Fuzz tests: random key-casing, numeric-as-string, null-vs-missing permutations
Performance benchmark: micro-bench adapter decision cost in detect-only vs suggest-and-log vs auto-adapt modes
SDK contract tests to ensure existing error.code and message remain stable for existing clients
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): deploy to staging runtime with detect-only; run discovery on 72h of replayed production traces
Phase 2 (pilot): enable suggest-and-log for 5 pilot customers; collect developer feedback and measure support ticket delta for function-call errors
Phase 3 (opt-in): release auto-adapt behind per-customer flag and policy; require customer acknowledgement in Console for any destructive transforms
Phase 4 (gradual default): if pilot metrics show >30% reduction in fix time and no safety incidents, flip default to suggest-and-log for new customers only
telemetry: Emit repairable_schema_error metrics: count, bucketed by model, route, transform_type, and mode
Histogram of confidence_score distribution for suggested_fixes
Counter for transforms applied in auto-adapt mode (coercions, defaults, renames)
Link repair incidents to support tickets via correlation_id when user opts-in to share telemetry
